claim: For every finite-dimensional multipartite state \(\rho\), the trace-norm optimization over the tensor-product partial-scaling maps \(T_{\lambda}=\frac{1+\lambda}{2}I+\frac{1-\lambda}{2}T\) of Lupo–Man’ko–Marmo–Sudarshan, with \(\lambda\in[-1,1]\) on any chosen set of parties, is attained at a cube vertex and equals \(2\max_S \mathcal N_S(\rho)\), where \(S\) ranges over the corresponding partial-transpose subsets. If scaling is applied to all but one party, this is exactly twice the largest ordinary bipartition negativity. Consequently every partially scaled operator is positive whenever all corresponding subset partial transposes are positive, so the continuous scaling parameters add no detection power beyond those ordinary PPT tests.

integrity: The proof is analytic and uses only tensor distributivity, nonnegative convex weights, trace-norm convexity, and invariance under full transpose.
The defining source was inspected at Eq. (18), the multipartite map Eq. (40), the trace-norm maximization Eqs. (50)-(51), and the conclusions.
The standard negativity definition and convexity were checked against arXiv:quant-ph/0102117.
limitations: The theorem applies only to the Eq. (18) identity-transpose scaling family and its tensor products, not to larger anisotropic positive-map families.
It identifies detection and trace-norm optimization with partial-transpose negativities; it does not make PPT sufficient for separability.
The literature search cannot exclude an obscure unindexed statement of the same convex-hull reduction.

title: The Eq. (18) partial-scaling optimization is exactly maximum bipartition negativity
